title: "Data Quality and IPA Research Protocols"

  Every research project at IPA is required to follow IPA's Research Protocols,
  also called the 'Minimum Must Dos' (MMDs), to ensure that IPA produces
  high-quality research. The protocols fall into three categories: Data Quality,
  Data Security and Research Ethics, and Knowledge Management and Transparency.
  IPA's DataSure and Data Management System (DMS) are the standard tools for
  meeting them. This page maps each protocol to the Knowledge Hub guidance that
  helps you comply.

## Research Protocols

IPA's Research Protocols are organized into three categories, plus the Data
Management System that IPA provides to help projects meet them. Each entry below
states the protocol, summarizes the requirement, and links to the Knowledge Hub
page that explains how to implement it.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Data Management System (DMS)

The [IPA Data Management System (DMS)](data-management-system.qmd) is not a
protocol itself. It is IPA's standard Stata and Excel toolkit for meeting the
data quality protocols below, covering high frequency checks, backchecks,
tracking, and progress reporting.

- [IPA Data Management System (DMS)](data-management-system.qmd)
- [Guide to IPA's Data Management System in Stata](how-to-dms-stata.qmd)
- [DataSure](datasure/index.qmd): IPA's dashboard for running the DMS checks
  without writing Stata code
- `ipacheck` (high frequency checks) and `bcstats` (backcheck comparisons) are
  the Stata programs behind the DMS. See [High Frequency
  Checks](high-frequency-checks.qmd) and [Backchecks](backchecks.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Data Quality

1. **Create survey plan before launch.** An operational plan covering timelines,
   staffing, logistics, and procurement for every survey stage, aligned with the
   project budget. See [Survey Planning](survey-plan.qmd).
2. **Create data quality assurance plan and materials before launch.** Set out
   requirements for backchecks, high frequency checks, accompaniments, spot
   checks, data flow, roles, reporting schedules, and triggered actions. See
   [Data Quality Action Plan](action-plan.qmd).
3. **Bench test survey (ideally at least two weeks in advance).** Test the
   programmed survey in the office with at least three different testers, and
   re-test after every change. See [Bench Testing](bench-testing.qmd).
4. **Pilot survey (ideally at least one week in advance).** Pilot every survey
   in communities outside the study sample, as close to real surveying as
   possible, including devices and data flow. See [Pilot
   Survey](pilot-survey.qmd).
5. **Accompany surveyors in first week of survey.** Field supervisors must
   personally accompany every field officer at least once during the first week,
   then scale down. See [Accompany Surveyors](accompany-surveyors.qmd).
6. **Implement and act on high frequency checks.** Run frequent checks on
   surveyor performance, ethics compliance, outliers, duplicates, and
   project-specific issues, with clear roles and triggered actions. See [High
   Frequency Checks](high-frequency-checks.qmd).
7. **Implement and act on backchecks.** Re-interview a random subset of
   respondents with a qualified backchecker, compare answers, and act on
   discrepancies. See [Backchecks](backchecks.qmd).
8. **Double enter and reconcile paper surveys.** If collecting paper surveys,
   two independent operators must enter each; a third reconciles discrepancies
   against the original. See [Data Integrity: Double
   Entry](data-integrity.qmd#double-entry).
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Data Security and Research Ethics

1. **Maintain IRB approval throughout project lifecycle.** Cover initial
   approval, renewals, amendments, unexpected event reports, and current human
   subjects certificates for everyone who can see PII. See [The IRB
   Lifecycle](/research-ethics/irb-lifecycle.qmd).
2. **Create data security plan and set up encryption before launch.** Respondent
   data must be encrypted at every stage from the moment of collection: device,
   transmission, server, cloud storage, laptops, and removable media. See [Data
   Security Protocol](/data-security/data-security-protocol.qmd).
3. **Maintain data security plan throughout project lifecycle.** Keep PII
   encrypted in storage and transit, and restrict passwords to essential IRB
   research staff. See [How to Implement Data Security
   Protocols](/data-security/how-to-data-security.qmd).
4. **Use new UID in deidentified dataset.** Before sharing or publishing
   unencrypted data, remove all identifying information and replace the original
   unique identifier with a new one. See [Data
   Anonymization](data-anonymization.qmd).
5. **Retire your project with all IRBs once the project is complete.** Close out
   with every reviewing IRB once interventions are finished and you no longer
   actively work with identified data. See [The IRB Lifecycle:
   Closure](/research-ethics/irb-lifecycle.qmd#closure).
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Knowledge Management and Transparency

1. **Back up data in at least two locations.** Keep at least two copies at all
   times, for example the SurveyCTO server plus a laptop synced to Box. Never
   delete server data until it has fully synced. See [Data Integrity:
   Maintaining Data Backups](data-integrity.qmd#maintaining-data-backups).
2. **Save all project files to long-term storage.** Store raw data,
   questionnaires, manuals, logs, high frequency check files, do-files, IRB
   documents, and replication code in the designated long-term storage following
   common folder structure. See [Data Integrity: Storing Files on
   Box](data-integrity.qmd#storing-files-on-box) for an example.
3. **Register project with AEA.** Register every IPA study in the American
   Economic Association's RCT Registry. A pre-analysis plan is not required. See
   [AEA RCT Registry](aea-registry.qmd).
:::

## Putting the Protocols into Practice

The protocols apply whether you hire your own surveyors or contract a survey
firm. A firm may carry out some steps, but IPA staff remain responsible for
verifying that each protocol is followed and for maintaining oversight of the
quality assurance process.

Implementing these steps visibly and early tells the survey team that high
quality data is the top priority. Showing surveyors from the start that you and
your monitors will run high frequency checks, backchecks, and accompaniments
helps prevent falsified surveys and reinforces adherence to field procedures.
Quality control can create tension with survey teams. You can reduce it by
explaining that while you trust them, you must be able to demonstrate to the
outside world that you took every step to obtain the highest possible quality of
data. These measures also reveal strengths and weaknesses among surveyors, so
the leadership team can give targeted feedback and training.

### Your Presence in the Field

As a team leader, spend time with your surveyors, especially at the beginning of
the survey period. Direct presence helps ensure surveyors conduct surveys
correctly, lets you observe how respondents understand questions, and helps you
learn about the community you are collecting data from. High frequency checks,
backchecks, and accompaniments then give you confidence in data quality for the
rest of the survey period.
